question: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:
In the EU, 8.3 times more people die from the cold than from heatwaves.

In 2024, the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre published data showing that, on average, 363 809 people die each year in Europe as a result of the effects of the cold and around 43 729 people as a result of the effects of heatwaves. There are, therefore, 8.3 times as many cold-related deaths as heat-related ones per year. Cold weather is thus the greatest temperature-related health problem in the EU. Nonetheless, the EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change focuses mainly on heat, droughts, heavy rain and floods. There is, however, no specific strand dealing exclusively or primarily with the health effects of cold temperatures. What is more, experts are concerned that the EU’s energy and climate policies, as well as the sanctions against Russia and the war in Iran, could lead to energy shortages in the coming autumn and winter, which could in turn create massive problems for the heating of homes. 1.
What measures will the Commission take to finally reduce the catastrophic number of cold-related deaths?
Why are there no comparable emergency plans to prevent cold-related deaths, as there are for heatwaves?
What measures will the Commission take to prevent a further increase in the number of cold-related deaths in the EU in the face of an impending energy shortage this autumn?
